import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’ll trace the swarm’s audio and linker flow, inspect how Bob renders research highlights, and compare playback designs. I’ll write an independent report with a recommended implementation and register it as a durable artifact.

I’m using `sase_repo` to inspect the linked repositories, `sase_memory_read` for the project’s artifact and macro conventions, and `sase_artifact` to register the report. I’ll keep the investigation independent of the other swarm reports.

The current flow has a timing gap: audio and the linker both start after the lead report, but audio does not trigger the linker. The Highlights hook also runs only when a report is first added. A link inserted after audio finishes could therefore miss the PDF entirely. I’m checking how to make publication reliable.

A plain MP3 link should survive Bob’s PDF conversion; an embedded HTML player will be lost in the LaTeX output. I also found that the existing podcast URL contains the feed’s secret token, and feed copies expire under retention. That URL is unsuitable for a durable report. I’m comparing private playback links with an Obsidian attachment route.

I’m leaning toward a small “Listen to the summary” row near the top, backed by an immutable private MP3 URL. One reliability detail needs explicit handling: SASE’s `%wait` unblocks only after success. Making the linker wait on audio would leave the report parked if audio fails, so the design needs a truthful failure result as well as a success handoff.

The rendering check passed: `bob highlights create --include-id` produced a PDF with the exact MP3 URL as a clickable link and preserved the Bob marker. The HTML audio player disappeared from the PDF, as expected.

The main recommendation is now clear: keep the presentation simple, and make the media identity, lifetime, and publication order explicit. I’ll distinguish the changes needed for the first working version from optional inline playback in Obsidian.

The report is written and registered as a durable snapshot. It recommends a compact listening link, immutable private audio storage, and an explicit media handoff before publication, with the requirement adjustments and failure cases called out.

I’m using the required `sase_final` skill to declare the research repository change before ending the turn.
